findings.claim: Regex literals still corrupt quote state. Valid JavaScript `const re = /`/;\n// TODO: fix` returns no hits because the regex backtick opens a persistent template-string state. Likewise, a regex containing an apostrophe hides a trailing same-line orphan comment. Recognize regex literals before processing quotes; the current regression test only covers recovery on the next line.

Resetting single/double quote state on every line incorrectly flags valid backslash-continued JavaScript strings. For source consisting of `const s = "hello\` followed by a newline and `// TODO: example";`, the second line is string data but is reported as an orphan. This can block the release gate and inflate the zero-baseline debt metric. Preserve quote state across genuine line continuations.

Go raw strings incorrectly use backslash escaping. In valid Go source with a backtick-delimited string ending in a backslash, the scanner treats the closing backtick as escaped, then silently ignores subsequent TODO comments until another backtick appears. Go raw strings do not interpret backslash escapes. Make quote handling language-aware in the template and generated checker.
